questions.question: Enumerate the health problems associated with poor eating habits in / adolescents.
questions.solution_html:
• Enumerate the health problems associated with poor eating habits in adolescents
  •  Skipping Meals
  •  Skipping meals deprives the body of essential nutrients such as proteins,iron,calcium and vitamins that are
  • needed for growth,energy and concentration
  •  As a result,it can cause fatigue,poor academic performance and reduced alertness
  •  It also leads to overeating later in the day,increasing the risk of obesity and digestive problems.
  •  Excessive consumption of Junk foods
  •  Junk foods are very low in essential nutrients like fibre,vitamins and minerals.
  •  Frequent intake of junk food can lead to obesity,hypertension,high cholesterol and even early onset of
  • diabetes
  •  Consumption of soft drinks and sugary beverages
  •  These drinks are loaded with sugar and caffeine,which contribute to obesity,tooth decay and disturbed
  • sleep patterns.
  •  They can also cause metabolic disorders and weaken bones because of decreased calcium intake.
  •  Consumption of foods containing trans fats and processed ingredients
  •  Trans fats increase bad cholesterol (LDL) and reduce good cholesterol(HDL),leading to obesity,heart
  • disease and fatty liver.
  •  They also trigger inflammation,hormonal imbalance and fatigue ,negatively affecting both physical and
  • mental health.
  •  Fad diets
  •  Prolonged adherence to such diets can cause nutritional deficiencies,weakness,hormonal disturbances and
  • even eating disorders such as anorexia and bulimia.
  •  These diets can interfere with normal growth and physical development during adolescence.
  •  Alcohol Consumption
  •  It affects brain development,impairs judgement and increases the risk of accidents
  •  Long term alcohol consumption can damage the liver,reduce appetite and interfere with nutrient absorption
questions.final_answer:  Long term alcohol consumption can damage the liver,reduce appetite and interfere with nutrient absorption
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the nutritional recommendations during Adulthood.
questions.solution_html:
•  Energy
  •  Caloric needs increase with the metabolic demands of growth and energy expenditure.
  •  Boys need 2860-3320kcal a day and girls need 2400-2500 kcal a day.
  •  Proteins
  •  Boys need 45-55gm/day while girls need 43-46gm/day
  •  This meets growth needs and for the pubertal changes in both sexes and for the developing muscle mass in
  • boys
  •  Fat and Essential Fatty acids
  •  The desirable level of visible fat intake for adolescents is 35-50g/d
  •  The essential fatty acid requirements is 3% E for adolescents.
  •  Minerals
  •  During adolescence,1000-1050mg of calcium and 1000-1050 mg of phosphorus per day is needed.Bone
  • growth demands calcium and phosphorus
  •  Boys require 22-26 mg/day and girls require 30-32mg/day of iron
  •  Zinc requirement is 14.3 to 17.6mg/day for boys and 12.8 to 14.2 mg/day for girls.
  •  Vitamins
  •  A daily allowance of 860-1000microgram of retinol is recommended for adolescents.
  •  600IU of Vitamin D is recommended for adolescents.
  •  Folacin and Vitamin B12 are essential for DNA synthesis .For all adolescents 2.2 microgram of Vitamin
questions.final_answer:  Folacin and Vitamin B12 are essential for DNA synthesis .For all adolescents 2.2 microgram of Vitamin
